assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction is a genuine instrument invention that opened a door: sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy, atom by atom, in TEM and STEM, now routine across materials science, catalysis, interfaces and quantum materials. It fits the mandate of a discovery or invention verified by experiment and used by many fields, and I judge it from the viewpoint of someone who works with these instruments.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical design of the correctors, Haider built and demonstrated the first working TEM corrector, and Krivanek did the same for STEM. These are the decisive original contributions in my understanding. The supplied credit omits Knut Urban, who is closely tied to the first corrected TEM and the Haider-Rose-Urban collaboration, so the allocation could be questioned; I do not add him because I may only use the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Correctors have been commercially available and independently reproduced for roughly two decades, and the technique is mature and stable. Recognition is overdue rather than premature, and this is not a lifetime-achievement case.
uncertainties: Whether a three-person prize can fairly omit Knut Urban, who is not in the credited names.
Whether the committee regards this as physics or as a tool for other fields; I believe the physics of electron optics is central, but this is my own judgement.
My recollection of the exact priority between the TEM and STEM correctors is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The flat bands at the magic angle, and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, created a new platform for quantum matter. The original experiment was clear, repeatable and followed by a large body of independent work.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat bands in 2011, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the original 2018 experimental discovery. The first author of those experiments, Yuan Cao, is not among the credited names, which is a real concern. The theory and the experiment together make a fair three-person prize if the committee accepts that structure.
assessment.maturity: The 2018 observations were reproduced by several independent groups within a few years, and the platform is now broad. Interpretation of the superconductivity remains unsettled, so the claim should rest on the flat bands and correlated states, not on the pairing mechanism.
uncertainties: Credit for the experimental team beyond the principal investigator, including the student who led the measurements.
The mechanism of superconductivity in magic-angle graphene is still debated.
Whether the field has matured enough, or whether waiting a few years would give a clearer verdict.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect form a basic concept in condensed matter, with the theoretical prediction followed by an experimental demonstration. It has lasting impact on topological materials and on ideas for spintronics and quantum devices.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 topological classification and the quantum spin Hall state in graphene. Molenkamp's group, building on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe. The Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang prediction and the Konig et al. experiment complicate the allocation, and others such as Fu, Kane and Hsieh in three dimensions also made important contributions; I use only the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many experiments in HgTe, InAs/GaSb and in the three-dimensional materials. The area is mature. The 2016 Nobel Prize for topological phase transitions covered related but distinct work, so this is not a duplicate.
uncertainties: Priority and fairness among Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and the three-dimensional topological insulator work.
Overlap with the 2016 prize for topological phases needs careful framing.
The practical impact beyond fundamental understanding is still modest.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level are a precision instrument that opens a door to tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The work is concrete, measurable and verified.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and demonstrated the first realization, and Ye's group pushed it to the 10^-18 level and developed the many-body spin-resolved systems. The pairing is plausible. Other groups, such as those in trapped-ion clocks, would be partly outside this candidate, and the 2005 prize already recognised frequency combs.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks agree at very high precision and the technology is increasingly used in international comparisons. The redefinition of the second is still pending, so the societal impact is not yet fully realised.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior recognition of optical frequency combs (2005 prize) and ion-trap work (2012 prize).
Whether the credit should also include other groups with independent early lattice-clock demonstrations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The LHC and its general-purpose detectors are among the largest and most successful instruments in physics, and they enabled the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson. I give weight to the invention and construction of the instrument, as the prize can honour inventions as well as discoveries.
assessment.attribution: Evans led the accelerator project, and Della Negra and Jenni were founding figures of CMS and ATLAS. Credit to a collaboration of thousands is hard to compress into three people, and the prize rules limit it. The decisive scientific contributions are distributed, so any selection will be contested; I would want to see the historical record of who proposed and led what.
assessment.maturity: The Higgs discovery in 2012 was confirmed independently by both experiments and by subsequent measurements. The theory was recognised in 2013. Recognition of the experimental side is timely, and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should honour the accelerator, the detectors, or the Higgs discovery itself.
Fair selection among many leaders of a very large collaboration; the candidate list shows a different set of names under the Higgs-discovery framing.
Overlap with the 2013 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultra-pure hexagonal boron nitride crystals are the substrate and encapsulant that made high-quality graphene and other van der Waals heterostructures possible, including fractional quantum Hall physics, moire materials and many device demonstrations. This is a materials enabler that I find compelling from a materials-physics view.
assessment.attribution: Watanabe and Taniguchi grew the crystals and are credited by essentially every group using them. The attribution is clear and the pair is natural, though they are not the discoverers of the underlying phenomena that use the crystals.
assessment.maturity: Impact is demonstrated across hundreds of independent experiments and the supply is stable. A prize here would be recognition of a materials platform rather than a single discovery, which is a question about the criteria.
uncertainties: Whether enabling-material growth counts as a discovery or invention under the mandate.
Whether the committee would prefer to recognise the physics enabled by the crystals instead.
Details of crystal growth priority are unverified by me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imaging a black hole shadow at horizon scale with an Earth-sized VLBI array is a major experimental achievement and a new instrument that opened a door to observing strong-field gravity directly. It is a clear verified result in 2019 and 2022.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept and Doeleman led the building of the global array and the collaboration. James Moran contributed significant VLBI pioneering work, but I would give weight to the proposers and leaders; this allocation is uncertain given a collaboration of hundreds.
assessment.maturity: The M87* and Sgr A* images are consistent and multi-epoch results are accumulating. The field is young, so further confirmation and independent analyses would strengthen the case, but the core result is robust.
uncertainties: Credit within a very large collaboration is hard to assign fairly.
Whether the results are mature enough for the prize or premature relative to later polarisation and time-resolved work.
The relative role of Moran versus Falcke and Doeleman is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The titanium-sapphire laser and the passive mode-locking schemes made the femtosecond solid-state laser a standard tool, supporting ultrafast spectroscopy, frequency combs and attosecond science. It is an invention with wide influence and verified performance, and it is a tool that opens doors for other research.
assessment.attribution: Moulton invented the Ti:sapphire laser medium, Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode-locking, and Keller invented semiconductor saturable-absorber mode-locking. These are distinct but connected inventions, and the three-person set seems reasonable. Other groups, such as Spence, Kean, and the early Kerr-lens work, may also need discussion. Including Keller also helps address the committee's wish to nominate more women, though this is not the reason for the ranking.
assessment.maturity: The technology has been in use for over three decades and is thoroughly verified. Recognition is not premature, though much of the downstream impact has already been honoured through the 2018 and 2023 prizes.
uncertainties: Priority for Kerr-lens mode-locking is shared with others not listed.
The prize may be seen as covering technology already recognised in related prizes.
Whether a compound candidate should be split among distinct inventions.
